target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures define the composition of Financial and Non-Financial Risk Management functions, their independence from business units, and their respective reporting lines to the Chief Risk Officer and Head of Non-Financial Risk. The 2025 text (ms_2025_7_P157_S001) aligns with the 2024 text (ms_2024_7_P265_S001) on this structural definition, despite the 2025 version adding specific function names (e.g., Climate Risk).

Both disclosures describe how the independent risk functions assist senior management (and the FRC/BRC) in monitoring and controlling risk through control processes and maintain their own risk governance structures. The 2025 text (ms_2025_7_P157_S002, S003) matches the 2024 text (ms_2024_7_P265_S002, S003) on these operational roles and governance aspects.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global Risk Management (GRM) organizational structure and independence
comparisons.peer_summary: Global Risk Management (GRM) operates as an independent control function led by the Chief Risk Officer (CRO), which is responsible for independently assessing and overseeing risks across FLUs and other control functions. GRM establishes enterprise policies for risk identification and control, supported by horizontal risk teams and vertical CRO teams that work collaboratively.
comparisons.comparison: Both Microsoft and Bank of America disclose that their independent risk management functions are structurally separate from business units and report to the Chief Risk Officer. Microsoft specifies that both Financial and Non-Financial Risk functions report to the CRO and Head of Non-Financial Risk respectively. Bank of America similarly states that Global Risk Management (GRM) operates as an independent risk management function led by the CRO and is part of control functions. Both emphasize the independence of these risk oversight functions from the business lines they monitor.

sentences.text: The Financial Risk Management functions (Market Risk, Credit Risk, Model Risk and Liquidity Risk Management Departments) and Non-Financial Risk Management functions (Compliance, Global Financial Crimes, and Operational Risk Departments) are independent of our business units and report to the Chief Risk Officer and Head of Non-Financial Risk, respectively.
GRM is part of our control functions and operates as our independent risk management function.
GRM, led by the Chief Risk Officer (CRO), is responsible for independently assessing and overseeing risks within FLUs and other control functions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Independent Risk Management culture and challenges
comparisons.peer_summary: Independent Risk Management, including the Operational Risk Management group, proactively works with businesses to drive an embedded operational risk culture and actively challenges the implementation and quality of risk management practices.
comparisons.comparison: Both Microsoft and Citigroup discuss the role of Independent Risk Management in supporting the business. Microsoft states that these independent functions report to the CRO and Head of Non-Financial Risk. Citigroup highlights that Independent Risk Management works proactively with businesses to drive an embedded operational risk culture and challenges implementation. While Microsoft focuses on the structural independence and reporting lines, Citigroup emphasizes the collaborative and challenging nature of the independent risk function's engagement with business units.

comparisons.peer_topic: Board Risk Briefings and CRO Reporting Structure
comparisons.peer_summary: The Board receives regular briefings from various officers on specific risk types (liquidity, market, credit, operational, model, climate, cybersecurity, compliance, legal, and reputational), with the chief risk officer reporting to the CEO and the Board's Risk Committee to advise on risk metrics and material exposures.
comparisons.comparison: Both Microsoft and Goldman Sachs disclose the reporting line of the Chief Risk Officer as part of the risk governance structure. Microsoft states that financial and non-financial risk management functions report to the Chief Risk Officer. Goldman Sachs explicitly states that the chief risk officer reports to both the chief executive officer and the Risk Committee of the Board, providing a similar high-level governance reporting structure to the Board and CEO, consistent with Microsoft's description of risk functions reporting to the CRO.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risk governance organizational roles and oversight
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm's Independent Risk Management (IRM) function, led by the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) and comprising Risk Management and Compliance, manages the risk governance framework. The CRO oversees Firmwide Risk Executives, Line of Business CROs, and the Chief Compliance Officer, with the framework approved by the Board Risk Committee.
comparisons.comparison: Both Microsoft and JPMorgan Chase describe their Independent Risk Management functions as distinct entities that manage risk governance. Microsoft notes that Financial and Non-Financial Risk Management functions are independent of business units. JPMorgan states that the Firm has an Independent Risk Management (IRM) function comprised of Risk Management and Compliance. Both companies structure their risk oversight separately from the business units to ensure independence.
